tasks.short: Prepare and present project status, risks, costs and decisions needed.

steps.what: Collect milestone progress, delivery dates and open issues from the {PROJECT}.
Reconcile the {ERP} cost export against the project budget in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Read team updates in the {EMAIL} and {CHAT} for risks and explanations.

loop.input: Project-scoped team updates and progress snapshot.
loop.output: Status notes with source references, dates and unresolved contradictions.
loop.check: Require a source for each claim; check dates and identifiers; flag conflicting accounts.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per reporting batch; unresolved items go to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Free-text updates describe causes and risks that fixed fields do not capture.

steps.what: Choose key messages and decisions for the presentation in the {DOCS}.
Build slides, charts and supporting detail in the {DOCS}.
Check accuracy, confidential detail and readiness to share the status presentation.
Present status and discuss decisions with the customer or project team.

tasks.design: A scheduled integration combines the {PROJECT} progress snapshot and {ERP} costs on the {DATA_PLATFORM}; a bounded loop extracts source-linked explanations from approved {EMAIL} and {CHAT} updates. A deterministic generator fills a presentation template in the {DOCS}, and the project manager approves disclosure and leads the discussion.
tasks.previous_blocker: Progress, costs and explanations sit in different places. Templates help layout but do not resolve conflicting updates.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing exports, stable project identifiers and cheaper integration development make assembly feasible. Bounded extraction can reduce reading while preserving source references.
tasks.still_hard: Late updates, disputed progress and politically sensitive messages still need investigation. Customer-facing claims require careful review.
tasks.human_edge: Choose which problem deserves attention and explain difficult trade-offs without losing trust.

ambition.what: A twice-weekly delivery recovery decision for threatened milestones.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from slide assembly toward investigating delivery risks and preparing recovery options. Approval and customer commitment rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Compare recovery options for a delayed milestone.
reach.learn: Scenario analysis, assumption testing and concise decision briefs.

evidence.claim: Project reporting can combine deterministic data assembly with bounded extraction of narrative updates.
A documented report failure involving invented sources supports source checks on generated narrative.

assumptions: The baseline is a mid-size European company with project tracking, finance exports and document templates.
Step shares and remaining time are planning estimates informed by the supplied priors.
Build ranges cover one reporting template and a limited set of source systems; they are working-day estimates.
Consultation time applies if staff-data use changes under national rules; elapsed approval time may be longer.
unknowns: Whether project and finance records share stable identifiers.
Which updates are approved for processing and which audiences may see them.
Whether existing reporting configuration already covers the presentation.
Which national rules and employee consultation requirements apply.
research_questions: Can existing {PROJECT} reporting populate the required presentation template?
How reliably does extraction preserve disagreement and source dates in representative updates?
new_work: Review extracted explanations and unresolved contradictions.
Maintain project mappings, template sections and audience permissions.
Check generated charts after source or budget changes.

tasks.short: Draft, approve, version and distribute project documents.

steps.what: Clarify the requested document, audience and deadline through the {EMAIL}.
Gather approved templates, project facts and prior decisions from the {DOCS} and {PROJECT}.
Draft project-specific explanations and instructions in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Approved document brief, template and source pack.
loop.output: Project-specific text with source references and explicit gaps.
loop.check: Validate required sections and source references; reject unsupported commitments; document owner checks meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per document; missing facts or disputed instructions return to the owner.
loop.why_not_simpler: Project-specific explanations need prose synthesis; fixed fields cover only the standard sections.

steps.what: Apply formatting, tables, identifiers and required sections in the {DOCS}.
Review the draft and approve its facts, instructions and commitments.
File the approved version and update the document register in the {DOCS}.
Check recipients and send approved document links through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: An intake form in the {WORKFLOW} selects the document template and gathers approved facts from the {PROJECT} and {DOCS}. A deterministic generator fills standard sections, while a bounded loop drafts project-specific prose; the {WORKFLOW} routes content approval, versions the result in the {DOCS} and sends links through the {EMAIL} after recipient approval.
tasks.previous_blocker: Source facts, templates and release lists are maintained separately. Project-specific prose and unclear document ownership interrupt standard workflows.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing versioning and approval configuration can handle much of the flow. Cheaper template and connector development makes the remaining assembly practical.
tasks.still_hard: Ambiguous instructions, contractual commitments and inconsistent source documents require an accountable owner. Legacy formatting can make generators costly to maintain.
tasks.human_edge: Determine whether instructions are usable, complete and within the project's authority.

ambition.what: A searchable handover pack for receiving operations teams.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts toward resolving document gaps and improving handovers. Document owners retain approval rights, and the project manager retains release responsibility.

reach.task: Maintain project document classification and retrieval.
reach.learn: Retention schedules, metadata design and permission management.
Approval routing, recipient controls and version discipline.

evidence.claim: Templates, version records and approval routing can automate routine document production and release.
Free-text drafting benefits from approved sources and a named reviewer.

assumptions: Documents include plans, instructions, minutes and handover material rather than a single document type.
The distribution step models a release that includes external recipients; internal releases use internal authority.
Build ranges cover a small initial template family and are working-day estimates.
GDPR applies to personal data; consultation under national rules is included where the processing changes.
unknowns: Which document types and templates are required.
Who can approve instructions and contractual statements.
Which recipients require external access and which retention rules apply.
Whether existing {DOCS} configuration supports approval, versioning and controlled links.
research_questions: Which document sections can be populated entirely from structured fields?
Can rendered documents preserve required layout and accessibility across the initial template family?
new_work: Review drafted prose and resolve missing source facts.
Maintain templates, metadata and approval routing.
Review recipient permissions and failed deliveries.
Retire outdated document versions and source material.

tasks.short: Negotiate project resources, materials, timing and commercial terms.

steps.what: Collect resource needs, delivery dates and purchase constraints from the {PROJECT} and {PROCUREMENT}.
Request availability and quotations from suppliers or internal resource managers through the {EMAIL}.
Compare availability, prices and conditions in the {SPREADSHEET}.

loop.input: Written resource offers and requirement fields.
loop.output: Comparable offer fields with source references and missing-term flags.
loop.check: Validate currencies, units and dates; calculate totals deterministically; verify unusual terms against sources.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair pass per offer; unreadable or ambiguous offers return to the project manager.
loop.why_not_simpler: Availability conditions and exclusions arrive in inconsistent prose and attachments.

steps.what: Agree negotiation limits and acceptable trade-offs with the project sponsor.
Negotiate availability, timing and terms with suppliers or internal resource managers.
Write agreed terms and unresolved points in the {DOCS}.

loop.input: Project manager's negotiation notes and provisional resource agreement.
loop.output: Agreement draft separating settled terms from unresolved points.
loop.check: Trace each term to notes; compare against the mandate; project manager checks meaning.
loop.stop: One draft and one repair pass per negotiation; disputed or missing terms require human clarification.
loop.why_not_simpler: Negotiation notes contain conditional agreements that do not fit fixed template fields.

steps.what: Approve and issue the supplier commitment through the {PROCUREMENT}.

tasks.design: The {WORKFLOW} gathers requirements from the {PROJECT} and {PROCUREMENT}, sends approved quotation requests through the {EMAIL} and builds a comparison using deterministic calculations plus bounded offer extraction. People set the mandate and negotiate; a bounded drafting loop prepares the agreement in the {DOCS}, and the {PROCUREMENT} approval flow controls the commitment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Requirements and offers arrive in different formats. Scarce resources and relationship-dependent concessions resist fixed rules.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured request flows and cheaper integrations reduce preparation work. Bounded extraction makes heterogeneous offers easier to compare.
tasks.still_hard: Internal priority conflicts, supplier leverage and conditional concessions remain human work. Commitments may need procurement or legal review.
tasks.human_edge: Read interests, build trust and trade price, timing and capacity within a clear mandate.

ambition.what: A cross-project capacity swap proposal for competing delivery teams.

tasks.altitude: The week contains less offer chasing and more preparation for difficult resource trade-offs. Negotiation limits and purchasing approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Assess alternative supply and capacity options.
reach.learn: Lead-time risk, total cost and supplier dependency.

reach.task: Check whether promised resource dates fit operational capacity.
reach.learn: Capacity calendars, sequencing constraints and escalation paths.

evidence.claim: Procurement policy checking and negotiation automation exist, but this does not establish suitability for project resource bargaining.
SUEZ reported reduced requisition cycle time and manual reviews in a vendor case; those results are not estimates for this task.
Offer preparation and agreement paperwork can change while relationship-dependent negotiation stays human.

assumptions: The baseline includes both supplier negotiations and internal resource negotiations.
The final commitment step models supplier purchasing; internal allocation instead requires the relevant resource manager's approval.
Automated quotation requests use approved contacts and templates and make no binding commitment.
Negotiations produce provisional terms pending commitment approval.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for one request and approval flow.
GDPR applies to contact and staff data; national consultation rules apply if resource-data processing changes.
unknowns: The project manager's negotiation and purchasing mandate.
Whether offers arrive in structured forms or attachments.
Which approval route applies to internal resource allocations.
Whether resource data includes individual employee evaluations.
Which national rules require employee consultation.
research_questions: Can existing {PROCUREMENT} configuration cover requests, comparisons and commitment approvals?
Which conditional offer terms most often cause comparison errors?
new_work: Verify extracted offer conditions and exceptions.
Maintain contact lists, request templates and mandate thresholds.
Check agreement drafts against actual negotiated terms.
Resolve requests that cross purchasing or resource-allocation limits.

tasks.short: Track project staff costs and investigate budget variances.

steps.what: Collect recorded staff time, booked costs and expenses from the {PROJECT}, {ERP} and {EXPENSE}.
Map project codes and cost categories and resolve duplicates in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Compare costs with the project budget and calculate variances in the {SPREADSHEET}.
Discuss unexplained variances and missing entries with the finance team and workstream leads.
Record the budget issue, owner and proposed response in the {PROJECT}.
Notify the project sponsor and finance team of the budget issue through the {EMAIL}.

tasks.design: An integration on the {DATA_PLATFORM} reconciles approved {PROJECT}, {ERP} and {EXPENSE} records and feeds a budget dashboard in the {BI}. Configured rules open exceptions in the {PROJECT} and notify approved internal recipients through the {EMAIL}; people investigate causes, while budget changes and accounting corrections follow their existing approval routes.
tasks.previous_blocker: Project codes, booking dates and cost definitions differ between sources. Manual reconciliation hides missing data and double-counted expenses.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduled exports and explicit mapping rules can replace repeated reconciliation. Existing dashboard and notification configuration covers much of the output.
tasks.still_hard: Unbooked time, delayed expenses and changing cost rates can distort the picture. A variance alone does not explain its cause or justify a staffing decision.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish timing differences from delivery problems and challenge assumptions with finance and technical leads.

ambition.what: A weekly corrective-action decision on unexplained staff-cost variance.

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from collecting and calculating costs toward investigating exceptions and preparing corrective options. Budget, staffing and accounting approval rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Explain cost drivers and test a revised project forecast.
reach.learn: Accruals, rate effects, forecast assumptions and sensitivity analysis.
Allocation methods and the limits of comparing unlike projects.

evidence.claim: Structured cost reconciliation, variance calculations and threshold alerts can use deterministic technology.
GDPR Article 22 concerns solely automated decisions with legal or similarly significant effects; cost reporting alone does not establish such a decision.
Dutch works-council consent provisions cover specified staff-data and monitoring arrangements; other countries require their own national-rule assessment.

assumptions: The baseline uses system records with a spreadsheet reconciliation layer.
Finance-approved cost rates are used instead of exposing individual payroll details.
Reports focus on project costs and do not score employee performance or decide staffing actions.
GDPR applies to personal data; EU AI Act classification needs reassessment if worker evaluation is later introduced.
Build ranges are working-day estimates for an initial cost feed, mapping and dashboard.
Access and consultation work is included; elapsed consultation time can exceed the estimated effort.
unknowns: Whether the {ERP} already provides a complete project-cost and variance view.
Where staff time and approved cost rates are held.
How expenses, accruals and posted costs overlap.
Which recipients may see staff-level versus aggregated costs.
Which national consultation rules apply to the proposed data use.
research_questions: Can existing {ERP} configuration eliminate the reconciliation layer?
Which reconciliation checks detect missing periods, duplicate expenses and stale rates?
What project-level aggregation still supports useful investigation?
new_work: Resolve unmapped costs, missing periods and duplicate records.
Maintain cost mappings, approved rates and alert thresholds.
Review access permissions and source-feed failures.
Explain false alerts caused by booking delays or accrual changes.

role.altitude: Project managers spend less time assembling documents and reconciling costs, and more time testing recovery options, resolving resource conflicts and preparing decisions. Sponsors, document owners and procurement managers retain their existing approval rights.
reach: Management analyst: compare recovery scenarios and explain project cost drivers.
Administrative assistant: coordinate approvals and controlled document distribution.
Supply chain manager: assess resource alternatives and delivery risk.
File clerk: improve project records, classification and retrieval.
skills_to_grow: Document permissions, retention and release controls.
GDPR and applicable national employee consultation rules.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a weekly project decision service that combines delivery risks, staff-cost variance and resource alternatives into concrete recovery options for sponsors.
